What the three routines do, and why the order is 0x70, 0x60, 0x84, is not observable from this body and is not claimed.

observed_mechanics: 0x00f96840 56 PUSH ESI -- the body's entire prologue. The record's saved_registers is [ESI] and nothing else, and parse.frame confirms no EBP frame, no SUB ESP and no local_extent.

0x00f96841 8b f1 MOV ESI,ECX -- the only read of ECX in the body, and the machine record names that register as the RECEIVER (receiver.register ECX, confidence INFERRED, shape R-ALIAS). The copy buys lifetime across two full calls; ECX is not written again until 0x00f9684f.

0x00f96843 8b 06 MOV EAX,dword ptr [ESI] -- the first of three reads of the receiver's offset 0x0. The value read is used as the base of the next displacement and is re-read before each of the other two transfers, so it is sampled fresh each time rather than cached.
0x00f96845 8b 50 70 MOV EDX,dword ptr [EAX + 0x70] -- the first of the three table displacements. 0x70 is the record's own dispatch reading; no member is named and no slot identity is claimed.
0x00f96848 ff d2 CALL EDX -- register-indirect, no stack argument pushed, no stack adjustment on either side, and nothing on any path skips it: the body has no branch.
0x00f9684a 8b 06 MOV EAX,dword ptr [ESI] -- the second read of the receiver's 0x0.
0x00f9684c 8b 50 60 MOV EDX,dword ptr [EAX + 0x60] -- the second displacement, 0x60.

0x00f9684f 8b ce MOV ECX,ESI -- ECX is re-established from the alias after the first call. Nothing about it is observable in this body beyond the fact that ECX holds the receiver again at the second call, which the receiver already guarantees.
0x00f96851 ff d2 CALL EDX -- the second register-indirect transfer, again with nothing pushed.
0x00f96853 8b 06 MOV EAX,dword ptr [ESI] -- the third read of the receiver's 0x0, and the value EAX holds when the body leaves.

0x00f96855 8b 90 84 00 00 00 MOV EDX,dword ptr [EAX + 0x84] -- the third displacement, 0x84, and the target of the tail jump. It is READ, not called, at this point; the transfer is four instructions later.

0x00f9685b c7 86 14 08 00 00 00 00 00 00 MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x814],0x0 -- the body's ONLY store, ten bytes wide, immediate zero, at the receiver's 0x814. receiver.written_through is 1 and receiver.max_offset is 2068 = 0x814, so this is both the only write and the furthest reach the record attributes to this body. It happens after both calls and before the transfer out, so the tail routine observes the zeroed word; the model test reads that word back at the moment of the transfer, which is the only place the ordering is observable.
0x00f96865 8b ce MOV ECX,ESI -- the receiver is handed to the tail routine in ECX, the third and last write to ECX.
0x00f96867 5e POP ESI -- the epilogue. It runs BEFORE the transfer out, so the tail routine is entered with the caller's stack exactly as it stood at the call and with ECX holding the receiver.

0x00f96868 ff e2 JMP EDX -- the transfer out. This is why abi_derived abstained ("no_terminal_ret: function has no RET instruction"), why cleanup.side and cleanup.bytes are null, and why no return type is determinable: whatever the caller eventually receives in EAX is this routine's, and it is outside this body.
semantic_findings: The body has no return. Its single transfer out is a tail jump through the word read at 0x00f96855, and that is the direct and sufficient reason the machine's derived ABI record abstained on the calling convention (ABI_UNKNOWN, confidence UNKNOWN, abstained_because "no_terminal_ret: function has no RET instruction"). A package that answered the convention question here would be answering it against the record's own stated refusal.

The receiver IS established independently of the convention: ECX, R-ALIAS into ESI, INFERRED, bounds-only, reaching exactly two displacements (0x0 and 0x814) and writing one. The convention abstention does not extend to the receiver, and the two facts are carried separately in the header and checked separately in the model test.

The record's own tail_call sub-record reads present false even though the last instruction is a tail transfer. Both are the same fifteen instructions seen from two directions -- the record sees the missing terminator, the listing sees the jump -- and this package reports both rather than treating the listing as correcting the record.

The three transfers are all two-level loads through the word at the receiver's +0x00, at displacements 0x70, 0x60 and 0x84, and the word is re-read before each. There is no direct callee and no rel32 operand anywhere in the 42 bytes, which is why the byte window can compare every position literally instead of resolving displacements.

The single store is the only write the body makes, it is at the receiver's 0x814, and its value is the immediate 0 read back from the full ten-byte encoding. It is also the only displacement through the receiver that the body writes, and it is the furthest the record attributes to this body (max_offset 2068).
unresolved_questions: The calling convention is undetermined and the machine record says so. All four candidates (__cdecl, __stdcall, __thiscall, __fastcall) remain open because the body has no terminator to read a cleanup from, and nothing in these 42 bytes separates a COM/__stdcall object from a __thiscall method. A caller-side observation, a this-adjusting entry stub, or a terminator in a neighbouring function would settle it; none of those is in this record.

The cleanup side and size are undetermined (cleanup.side null, cleanup.bytes null, confidence UNKNOWN). There is no RET immediate to be either, and the body pushes nothing and reads nothing on the stack, so there is no argument to account for either.

No return type is determinable. The only exit belongs to the routine at table slot 0x84, which is outside this body, so what the caller receives in EAX is that routine's return. The record says the same: return.type null, void_possible false, and a machine return state of UNCLASSIFIED on a body with a tail exit.

The receiver's identity is unresolved: no size, no layout, no member, no vtable-pointer offset, no owning class. bounds_only true and shape R-ALIAS are the record's own limits, and the body neither adjusts nor tests the pointer, so whether ECX points at the head of an object or an interior sub-object is invisible here.

What the three routines at table slots 0x70, 0x60 and 0x84 do is unknown, as is why that order. The order is transcribed; the reason is not observable from this body. The record associates this address with vtable 0x01490be8, but the binary carries no MSVC RTTI and no SDK name is recorded for that table, so no class, vtable identity or slot name is claimed.

The meaning of the word the body loads at 0x00f96843 beyond "it is the base of the next displacement" is unknown. The model treats it as a table pointer because that is the only use the fifteen instructions make of it, and it does not claim the object's own vtable identity from that.
No original-process trace exists in this repository, so nothing here is runtime-validated. Every statement in this record is a static reading of the image and of the machine's own derived ABI record.
